questions.q: What is a restaurant reputation management tool?
questions.a: It's software that monitors reviews and mentions across review sites, social media and other channels, so you know how the public sees your restaurant. It brings mentions, comments and other activity that needs attention into one place, then helps you respond. That saves a lot of time when your brand appears on many platforms.

questions.q: Why does a restaurant need reputation management?
questions.a: Guests have plenty of options, and reviews shape whether they give your restaurant a try. A run of bad reviews left unanswered can hurt you for a long time, because opinions formed from reading reviews are hard to change. Managing your reputation helps you stand out, respond to criticism on time and keep new guests coming.

questions.q: Should I respond to both positive and negative reviews?
questions.a: Yes, respond to reviews whatever their sentiment. For a negative review, acknowledge the problem, apologize and invite the guest to give you another chance. For a positive one, go beyond a plain thank you with a personal touch and an invitation to come back.

questions.q: How can I stop complaints from turning into public reviews?
questions.a: Give guests a direct, private way to share feedback, such as a QR code survey on table stands, cards in delivery bags or printed receipts. That lets you resolve problems one to one and grow your customer database at the same time. Better service, informed by what that feedback tells you, reduces complaints over time.

questions.q: What else helps a restaurant's online reputation?
questions.a: Keep your Google Business Profile complete, with an accurate address, contact details, good photos and correct opening hours. Keep offers consistent across every platform, and maintain an active social media and website presence. Partnering with local media and food creators can also introduce you to new guests.
